name: The Road In
description: Every check in this scene is opportunistic and costs nothing on any result -- a-flourish is pure texture, the other two are Encyclopaedia checks that only ever add information, never take it away.

dc.basis: level 1 DC 15, one step easy — this is a treat, not a test

outcomes.criticalSuccess: It's genuinely cool, and somebody in the queue notices.
outcomes.failure: A small, funny stumble — a dropped kickstand, the wrong door, nothing that matters.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Comically embarrassing, entirely harmless — it stalls right in front of everyone.

dc.basis: level 1 DC 15, one step hard — most of the table won't get this, and that's the point

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Not the first one they've seen — always this exact deep violet, always at head height, always somewhere a crowd stops and waits. This one looks fresher than the others.
outcomes.success: It isn't the first one they've noticed today, now they think about it. Always the same deep violet. Always at head height.
outcomes.criticalFailure: They peg it confidently as a condemned-building notice, the kind the housing office stencils on empty lots. It isn't, and nobody around them corrects it.

dc.basis: level 1 DC 15, no adjustment — this is offered to the whole table, not a specialist's roll

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Everything in success, plus one more thing: it's moving carefully. More carefully than a war machine built to punch through a wall has any obvious reason to. Whoever's inside is minding something.
outcomes.success: A Directorate Frame — three storeys of plate and cable, moving like it genuinely weighs what it weighs. Not fast. Each step lands with a beat you feel in your chest before you hear it, hydraulics hissing at the knee and shoulder joints, the whole silhouette rolling forward with a slight, deliberate list, like something built to survive being wrong-footed rather than to never be. Steam or exhaust vents somewhere along the spine on the exhale of every stride. Up close it would swallow the road; from here it's simply part of the skyline doing a job — patrolling, hauling, holding up the structural work nothing smaller can reach. A gull lands on one shoulder plate mid-stride and doesn't bother leaving. Common enough along the coast that nobody nearby looks afraid of it.
outcomes.failure: Big. Loud, in the way the ground is loud. That's all anyone gets from this far off.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Called with total confidence as derelict — mothballed, kept for scrap, no one's home. It very much is not, though nothing about it right now proves that wrong.

notes:
a-flourish is never mandatory and never worth offering more than once per player; if nobody wants it, the scene loses nothing.

A check about a mitflit trap glimpsed on arrival was cut entirely 2026-09-09 -- see ideas/story/bible/species/mitflits.md for why (it read as this society normalising harm to a sentient species, and turned out to be factually wrong about the setting besides). Replaced 2026-09-09 with two opportunistic Encyclopaedia checks pulled from the story bible's own Mystery Ledger rather than invented fresh: a-mark-at-head-height (Ledger #6, the cicada stencils -- pays off Ch5) and a-frame-at-a-distance (raw material for Ledger #11, a Frame's odd gentleness -- pays off Ch3/Ch6, but only on a critical success here). Offer either to any player whose own arrival plausibly passes the trigger, and let anyone at the table roll who wants to, not only that player.
